children: Wholesale-price inflation sped up in August, the Labor Department said Thursday.
The producer-price index rose by 0.4% last month, versus its 0.1% increase in July. The reading was in line with economists' forecasts.
Over the 12 months through August, producer-price inflation was 5.4%.

The August report has been eagerly anticipated because some of its data, including price indexes for medical services and airfare, are used alongside consumer-price-index numbers to tabulate the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation metric, the personal-consumption expenditures price index.

The Fed's decision on whether or not to raise interest rates next week could well hinge on the precise August PCE inflation reading, so analysts will be poring over Thursday morning's data to update their estimates of that metric. By later this morning, they should have a clear idea of how the key PPI categories affected the gauge the Fed targets.
Estimates will remain cloudy, however, until economists can further incorporate Friday morning's August consumer-price data into their analysis.
